failure_summary: render_bug: the L3 causal-link text supplied by causalLinks.mjs asserts verbatim "Your opponent's threat to make four next move at c1r4 is coming no matter what you play here" and offers term:immediate_threat ("completes on the very next move") bound to truthBoard "decision", but on the decision board (movestring 3321133345501122252551125036666) column 1 has height 2 so c1r4 is a NON-gravity major threat ([X] in visualize_board, and the render's own decision-board tactics line correctly reads "major at c1r4 (opp)"); the same link's guardrail ("MUST NOT say the played move caused or enabled the pattern") suppresses the one real cause — playing column 1 fills c1r3 and turns c1r4 gravity-top (afterPlayed tactics line: "immediate at c1r4 (opp)", visualizer <*> [GT]) — so all 5 runs restate the outcome ("only speeds up the finish") instead of the cause and fail A7a.
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 are null for those axes (not scored, not passed). A5 and A7 graded on all 5. A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_subset_2026-08-26T15-47-56Z_mechanical.json (all pass). Model is gpt-5.4-mini = the production model, so this is a PRODUCTION-FIDELITY run: any prompt_confusion attribution here cannot be separated from model capability; I therefore lead with the model-independent render attribution. | A4 runs 0-1 FAIL: both say the opponent has a "threat to make four next move" at c1r4; false on the decision board (ht col1 = 2, next drop lands c1r3), true only after the played move. Runs 2 and 4 carry the same falsehood ("immediate threat", "next-move four") but were not scored for A4 under sub-sampling; run 3 avoids it ("your opponent's finishing square"). | A5 run 1 FAIL (A5a): raw cNrM notation in coach prose — "a threat to make four next move at c1r4, on the four-in-a-row line running through c4r1, c3r2, c2r3, and c1r4" — despite the prompt's explicit "Never write a raw square". This is the already-filed OI-194, not a new finding; triage prompt_confusion under the production-fidelity caveat. Runs 0, 2, 3, 4 use plain referring phrases and pass A5. A5b is N/A (boardState = closing, not opening). | A7 FAILS on all 5 runs, sub-test A7a only: none of the 5 names why column 7 resists or why column 1 is worse; every run ends on an outcome restatement ("gave them a cleaner path to that same finish", "lets the finish come faster", "leaves them with the same finish faster", "gets to convert it with less resistance", "gives them the cleanest follow-up"). The causal step IS derivable from the prompt (decision board "major at c1r4" vs afterPlayed "immediate at c1r4"), but the L3 text plus its guardrail steer away from it. A7b passes (every referring phrase is wrapped in an emitted zone resolving to c1r4 or the c4r1-c3r2-c2r3-c1r4 line). A7c is N/A (the mechanism is a single threat, not a fork; no *-fork-pivot handle was needed). A7d passes marginally ("toughest defense" idea anchored to the named squares). | G4 runs 0-1 PASS: every named cell checked against render_decision.finalMovestring 33211333455011222525511250366660 — c4r1, c3r2, c2r3 are all opponent (P1/X) discs and c1r4 is the empty completing square; no alternate PV was used. G5 PASS: every rendered threat-list entry is board-true on its stated board (decision "major at c1r4 (opp)", "major at c1r5 (you)", "major at c5r3" both, "major at c5r4 (you)"; afterPlayed "immediate at c1r4" both — all confirmed against visualize_board). G3 PASS: afterBest was omitted as shown:false and no answer needed it (its tag set is identical to the decision board). G6 PASS: patternOnAfterBestBoard=true with route realized_denied routes to L3, and the c1r4 major does survive on the after-best board 33211333455011222525511250366666. G7 PASS on all 5: annotationRepairs is empty everywhere, mechanical G7a/G7b membership passed, and every emitted handle matches its role shape — single-square words on [zone:c1r4], line words on [zone:windows:c4r1,c3r2,c2r3,c1r4]; note all 5 runs emit the SPEC form rather than the opp-major / opp-major-line handle names, which the resolver accepts (zero repairs). | Not intermittent: A7a fails 5/5 and the A4 defect is present in 4/5 texts. | OI-183 caveat: the harness calls the model once with no production retry, but that is not load-bearing here — the required set (opp-major, opp-major-line) was emitted in all 5 runs, so nothing would have been retried.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: causalLinks.mjs L3 text + zones.terms[immediate_threat].canonicalPhrase ("threat to make four next move" / "completes on the very next move"), bound to truthBoard "decision"
counterexamples.evidence: On 3321133345501122252551125036666 column 1 holds 2 discs, so the next drop lands c1r3 and c1r4 is a NON-gravity major threat ([X] in visualize_board; the prompt's own decision-board tactics line reads "major at c1r4 (opp)", not "immediate"). It only becomes gravity-top (<*> [GT], "immediate at c1r4 (opp)") after the played move on 33211333455011222525511250366660.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: link.guardrail ("MUST NOT say the played move caused or enabled the pattern") on L3
counterexamples.evidence: The decisive cause of the faster loss is that playing column 1 fills c1r3 and makes the opponent's standing diagonal c4r1-c3r2-c2r3-c1r4 immediately playable — the exact delta between the two rendered tactics lists (decision "major at c1r4" vs afterPlayed "immediate at c1r4"). The guardrail forbids the enabling framing and the link text substitutes "only speeds up the finish", so all 5 runs restate the outcome and none names the cause.
